items.title: Wilson "Chembo" Corniel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: See I play with Grady Tate and he’s a singer, and lightly. I don’t even have to put my hand on the conga, the full hand on it. I just do my fingertips just to get a little sound, enough to back him up without overpowering him.

ctx.x: Did you grow up with this just as part of the fabric of your childhood?

It is part of it, but the thing is when I was born and raised in New York City so I had all these other influences around me, you know, like I grew up with the Beatles, Motown, Glen Campbell, Willie Nelson, the Temptations, Rolling Stones. You know so it’s a whole mixture of different things besides my Latin roots that I picked up at home, the records that my mother played, the Tito Rodriguez, Machito, all the ballad singers, you know, so that’s always been in my ear, the Latin part, besides my surroundings…

with the Latin people there, we go out of our way to learn jazz traditionally. You know we go and spend the time so when we’ve got to set up and do a jazz gig it’s going to sound like a jazz gig. It’s not going to sound like a watered down fake chords, you’re gonna know the theory behind what you’re doing and stuff, so you can go out and play authentically. You’re not going to wash it down. You know each style of music — if I’m going to study flamenco music it’s going to be the traditional style. If I’m going to…
